question: Does the Lawaan river-fish poster provide a publication-ready, freshwater-only species inventory for Eastern Samar?

sourceReviewed.citation: Gacura, J. R. L. (2018, May). Fish Composition and Distribution in the Rivers of Lawaan, Eastern Samar, Philippines. Poster presented at the 5th Undergraduate Research Symposium; author-uploaded full poster hosted by ResearchGate.
sourceReviewed.access: Reviewed the ResearchGate record and the author-uploaded poster text. The record points to a UP Libraries TUKLAS catalog item (UP-1685675941123958185), but that item could not be independently opened during this review. The poster PDF is not copied into the repository.

reportedScope.coverageLimit: The poster says Lawaan has seven river systems but reports sampling only in Poblacion and Bolusao Rivers; it does not cover the other five rivers.
reportedScope.samplingWindow: October-November 2017 and January-February 2018; the poster describes this as a four-month assessment.
reportedScope.methods: Double gill nets, spears, and hooks-and-lines. Exact reach/site coordinates, station-level gear and effort, and water salinity are not reported in the accessible abstract/poster text.
reportedScope.reportedCatchAndRichness: 205 individuals and 41 species in Poblacion River; 54 individuals and 15 species in Bolusao River. The poster reports a between-river similarity index of 0.39; do not add the separate richness values into a unique two-river total without the full crosswalk.

sourceMentionedTaxa.claimAsPrinted: Most abundant in Poblacion River, 16.58% relative abundance.
Most abundant in Bolusao River, 18.52% relative abundance; also reported widely distributed in Poblacion River.
Appears in the poster's fish migration/resident table for Poblacion River; this is a source-reported lead only and does not confirm the separate Dupon River abstract identification.

reportedScope.otherReportedResult: The poster reports Ambassis interrupta, Moolgarda perusii, and Chelonodon patoca as widely distributed in Poblacion River, and Chelonodon patoca as widely distributed in Bolusao River. These are historical poster claims, not current presence or catchability findings.

crossSourceAssessment.habitatScope: The poster frames its work as freshwater-fish research, but does not provide site coordinates or salinity/tidal context. It also reports migratory groups including oceanodromous fishes and names taxa with broad aquatic habitats. Do not treat every record as confirmed freshwater-only until sampling stations and habitat context are reconciled.
crossSourceAssessment.relationshipToOtherSamarEvidence: This is a distinct, site-specific Lawaan study and is not the Samar Island Natural Park nine-river project. The earlier Samar review excluded it from freshwater-only inventory counts; this source review records that boundary explicitly.
crossSourceAssessment.inventoryReadiness: Research lead only. Although the poster reports river-specific richness, the accessible poster text does not provide a complete, auditable species-by-river-by-reach dataset with specimen/voucher identifiers and effort. Do not normalize the poster's figures into species, occurrence, geometry, diet, safety, legal, or catchability app records.
crossSourceAssessment.appReadiness: Not approved for public app use. The author-uploaded poster is marked as potentially copyrighted; no item-specific license or derivative-data reuse permission was found.

rightsReview.status: ResearchGate states that the poster content may be subject to copyright. No open license or item-specific reuse permission was identified.
rightsReview.handling: Retain citation metadata and a short source-bounded summary only. Do not copy the poster, its illustrations, full species list, figures, or table into the repository or app.

disposition.reason: Historical poster data cover only two of seven Lawaan rivers, do not establish freshwater salinity/reach context, and lack a complete independently auditable site-to-taxon and voucher crosswalk. Reuse terms are unresolved.

nextActions: Seek the original high-resolution poster or underlying thesis/report from the author or UP Visayas Tacloban, including the full 41- and 15-species lists, unique cross-river list, station/reach mapping, collection effort, and voucher/catalog identifiers; do not send an inquiry without explicit authorization.
Request permission and attribution terms before reproducing any poster-derived list, figure, or table in Bangwit.

Keep Poblacion and Bolusao evidence separate, and keep freshwater, brackish/estuarine, and marine-migrant claims distinct unless the site and salinity records support a classification. Continue the Eastern Visayas sweep across unreviewed Leyte, Samar, and Biliran waters.

sources.supports: Author-uploaded poster record and accessible poster text: author, May 2018 conference, sampling windows and gear, catch/richness summaries for the two rivers, selected reported taxa and distribution claims, and copyright caveat.
